{{Quote|We'll let fate decide.|[[Watto/Legends|Watto]]|<ref name="Episode 1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
A '''chance cube''', also known as a '''die''' (pl. '''dice'''), was a small, frequently—but not always—cubical object used for [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] or making 'A or B' decisions. Most common dice were cubes giving only two results after being thrown; three of its sides were one color, while the other three were another color.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref> Some dice were weighted by less sporting owners as it was more easily 'tempered' than a flipped coin.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>

==History==
[[File:Chance_Cube_Celebration_EotE_CR.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] celebrates his victory in a chance cube game]]
{{Quote|I just happen to have a chance cube here. Blue&mdash;it's the boy. Red&mdash;his mother.|Watto, deciding whether to wager Anakin Skywalker or his mother in a bet|<ref name="Episode 1" />}}
[[Watto/Legends|Watto]] used a chance cube he had with him to gamble with [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] on the outcome of the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]]. He refused to bet both [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and his mother [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi]] against [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's Podracer]], claiming that no Podracer was so expensive it could cover the value of two slaves in a bet. Instead, he proposed to roll his chance cube to decide which [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] would be wagered: blue for the boy, red for his mother. Qui-Gon Jinn used [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]] to influence the fall of the chance cube to ensure that Anakin's freedom would be at stake.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /> As Watto had weighted the die to land on red, and had five red spaces and one blue, to ensure winning such random tosses, Jinn's trick took him quite by surprise.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace (novelization)" /> (Note: in the film, Watto's cube appears to be the standard arrangement: 3 red sides and 2 blue sides are visible as it rolls; the sixth side is never seen. Based on Watto's shocked reaction at the result, it is likely that it was weighted for red)

[[Vilmarh Grahrk]] once played a game with chance cubes in a casino on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]], although these had more than six sides.<ref name="Star Wars Republic: Rite of Passage">''[[Star Wars: Rite of Passage]]''</ref>

[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] had a [[Han's dice|pair of dice]]-shaped ornaments decorating the cockpit of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

[[King/Legends|King]] [[Katuunko/Legends|Katuunko]] also used a Chance Cube to choose [[Rugosa/Legends|Rugosa]] for a diplomatic meeting on whether he should join the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] or the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="Ambush">{{TCW|Ambush}}</ref>

During a mission to the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] in [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]], [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Saba Sebatyne]] and [[Tekli]] played a dice game while on board the ''[[Jade Shadow]]''. Their [[Infrared/Legends|infrared]]-readable dice cubes appeared simply black to the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Eye/Legends|eye]].<ref name="FH 1">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic I: Remnant]]''</ref>

In [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]], [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Alec (Jedi)|Alec]] gambled with chance cubes in the [[Grande Game]] casino of [[Depatar/Legends|Depatar]], winning so many times that the owner retired the table for maintenance.<ref name="cp">{{LivingForce|Clouds of Genarius: Clouded Paths}}</ref>
